newsitem.title: UK: Smaller firms lead the UK manufacturing pack - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Smaller firms lead the UK manufacturing pack - CBI.

text.p: Smaller British manufacturing firms are outperforming the rest of the industry, top employers organisation the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.

The CBI's survey of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), conducted with chartered accountants Pannell Kerr Foster, showed SMEs enjoyed the highest increase in total orders for a year even though export orders fell as the pound pushed relentlessly higher.

The survey showed a positive balance of 11 percent of firms reported an increase in domestic orders over the past four months -- 35 percent of firms reported higher orders, 26 percent said orders fell.

"Our survey paints a relatively upbeat picture, with small and medium enterprises outperforming the manufacturing sector as a whole in terms of new orders and creating jobs," said Tony Bonner, chairman of the CBI's SME council.
Export orders are expected to pick up moderately over the next four months but expectations are the least positive since July 1993.

Prices as a factor likely to limit export orders over the next four months rose to its highest level in six years. The pound has jumped more than 13 percent, measured against a basket of other major currencies, since August last year.

"The increase in new orders is driven by domestic demand but the export market is becoming a matter of concern with sterling's strength beginning to hit exporters' orders and denting their confidence in their prospects overseas," Bonner said.
A positive balance of seven percent of SMEs reported a rise in employment over the past four months.
Overall, manufacturing industry produced a negative balance of 11 percent of companies reporting an increase in workforce.
The survey covered 902 manufacturing companies with fewer than 500 employees.
